report_ready_prose.preferred_primary: ICES with separate DOM, sediment POM and Discards and EE floor ON at 0.1 is the user-selected primary model. Its declared North Sea domain better matches LME_022, and keeping distinct detritus costs preserves the source compartment structure and avoids adding the common-cost assumption.
report_ready_prose.source_port_limitation: This is the published North Sea Rpath port snapshot. It materially differs from the accepted native ICES EwE Key Run, whose database was not obtained; native numerical equivalence is not established. Better geographic coverage and closed runtime budgets do not resolve this source-version limitation.
report_ready_prose.geography: The declared IVa-IVb-IVc footprint covers approximately 87% of LME_022, compared with approximately 40% for East Coast Scotland (37–42% source-map sensitivity). These are boundary interpretations, not statistical confidence intervals or recovered native grids.
report_ready_prose.time_transfer: ICES static 1991 and Scotland 1991–1995 coefficients are applied to 2019 catch. This is a historical-model transfer comparison, not an independently fitted 2019 ecosystem reconstruction.
report_ready_prose.source_scopes: All-source sums the returned PP, detritus and synthetic-import columns. PP-only is the within-model primary-producer column contribution and is a component of all-source, not an alternative full-budget total. Do not label all-source as purely photosynthetic production demand or conclude that ICES is lower/higher without stating the scope.
report_ready_prose.pooling: The supported always-collapse option calculates one shared detritus SPPR a/(1-b) for DOM (67), POM (68) and Discards (69). It retains all 70 runtime IDs, diets, fate routing and internal discard returns. It neither merges the canonical groups nor assumes a simple average of their former coefficients. Treat it as a common-cost sensitivity.
report_ready_prose.floor: EE floor 0.1 is a hypothetical nonfishery mortality-export assumption applied after audited initialization, with effective detritus stock closure and operational detritus EE = 1. It is not a source correction or renewed researcher approval.
report_ready_prose.diagnostics: All four cases pass strict model mass-balance and SPPR-budget checks. ICES GE/TE remain WARN: the separate diet-normalization check fails at max deviation 8.32503e-5; GE detritus feedback remains high, and TE has five near-zero-efficiency groups. Do not describe strict model balance as false because a separate diet check warns.
report_ready_prose.confidence: Confidence exposure here weights existing overall mapping categories by the same method-specific PPR denominator. It is not a probability or confidence interval. Scotland’s coarser groups have fewer stage splits; its larger High share does not establish whole-North-Sea applicability or superior source equivalence.
report_ready_prose.scotland_structure: Scotland has one detritus pool and no explicit internal-discard return matrix, whereas ICES retains separate coupled detritus and source-backed catch returns. Scotland’s historical TE b = 0 is a no-recycling convention and is not comparable to the ICES coupled rho_B.
report_ready_prose.settings_comparability: The fresh Scotland floor ON/OFF controls use the same frozen 38cb75d engine as ICES; OFF SPPR/A/L exactly reproduce the historical corrected matrices. Historical engine-version confounding has therefore been checked, while model structure, source-specific initialization, geography and mappings still differ.
report_ready_prose.scotland_signature: The preserved Scotland review says MODEL VALIDATED, Ido Carmel, 14/11/2026, and excludes Seabirds, Seals and Cetaceans, all due to GE < 0.01. No current mapped catch uses those recipients, so applying these exclusions removes zero regional catch/PPR. The trophic nodes remain; this is not a post-exclusion network solve and the signature does not approve the new floor ON sensitivity.
report_ready_prose.coverage: Common support is 372 taxa and 2,717,197.2863294235 t catch. ICES maps all 384 taxa and 2,717,260.6982051707 t. Scotland has 12 unresolved labels, 8 with positive catch totaling 63.4118757471 t; their model PPR stays unknown. Zero-catch unresolved labels have annual contribution zero but unknown coefficients.
report_ready_prose.decision_scope: Local primary-model choice is separate from researcher signature, mapping adoption and central publication. Project.xlsx, map and trends updates remain deferred by the user; this evidence handoff performs none of those actions.
